body.statement:
Fix \(n\), \(G\), \(r\), and a deterministic returned map \(F_G\), assume that \(\mathcal C_G(\delta_{\mathrm{chart}},\kappa_{\mathrm{chart}},K_{\mathrm{chart}},\nu_{\mathrm{chart}})\neq\varnothing\), and use the total pole and singular-covariance conventions in \(\mathrm{def:plug\mbox{-}in\mbox{-}estimator}\) and \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous\mbox{-}wald\mbox{-}set}\). Uniformly over \(\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G(\delta_{\mathrm{chart}},\kappa_{\mathrm{chart}},K_{\mathrm{chart}},\nu_{\mathrm{chart}})\),
\[
\sqrt N\{\widehat\theta_G-F_G(s)\}=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{IF}_F(X_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,V_F),\qquad \widehat V_F\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}V_F.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}\!\left\{\min_{1\le j\le r}|Q_{F,j}(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)|=0\right\}\to0,\qquad \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}\{\widehat V_F\text{ is singular}\}\to0.
\]
Consequently \(\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}\{F_G(s)\in\mathcal W_{G,N}(1-\gamma)\}\to1-\gamma\). The result covers every fixed finite vector of rational formulas returned by the total schedule on the Gaussian submodel; it makes no efficiency claim.
body.justification: A symbolic inverse becomes empirically usable only after its full joint first-order law and simultaneous coverage are supplied.
body.gap: Mareis, Sturma, and Drton treat fixed half-trek estimators, whereas the returned map here may be any deterministic rational quotient produced by degree-bounded elimination; Drton and Xiao show why the nondegeneracy boundary cannot be ignored.
body.consumer: An analyst can report simultaneous confidence regions for all structural coefficients returned by the exact stopping schedule on a declared regular chart.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(m=n(n+1)/2\), \(\widehat s=\operatorname{vech}(\widehat\Sigma)\), and
\[
 Y_i=\operatorname{vech}(X_iX_i^{\mathsf T}-\Sigma).
\]
The linear model with centered Gaussian disturbances gives \(X_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)\).  From the definition of the sample covariance,
\[
 \widehat s-s=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i-\operatorname{vech}(\bar X\bar X^{\mathsf T}). \tag{11}
\]

Let \(\mathcal C_G\) abbreviate the nonempty chart in the statement.  The eigenvalue restrictions put it inside the compact set \(\{\Sigma:\kappa_{\mathrm{chart}}I_n\preceq\Sigma\preceq K_{\mathrm{chart}}I_n\}\).  The denominator and nondegeneracy restrictions are closed because polynomials, rational derivatives away from their poles, Gaussian fourth moments, and eigenvalues are continuous.  Hence \(\mathcal C_G\) is compact.  If \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_n)\), write \(X=\Sigma^{1/2}Z\).  The upper eigenvalue bound then gives, for every fixed \(k\),
\[
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\mathbb E_\Sigma\|X\|^k
 \leq K_{\mathrm{chart}}^{k/2}\mathbb E\|Z\|^k<\infty. \tag{12}
\]
In particular, Chebyshev's inequality applied coordinatewise in (11) and to \(\bar X\) yields, uniformly on the chart,
\[
 \|\widehat s-s\|=O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \sqrt N\|\bar X\bar X^{\mathsf T}\|=O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-1/2}). \tag{13}
\]

By compactness, continuity of the finitely many \(Q_{F,j}\), and the margin \(\min_j|Q_{F,j}(s)|\geq\delta_{\mathrm{chart}}\), there is an \(\eta>0\), independent of \(\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G\), such that
\[
 \|t-s\|\leq\eta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \min_j|Q_{F,j}(t)|\geq\delta_{\mathrm{chart}}/2. \tag{14}
\]
On the compact tube in (14), all first and second derivatives of the fixed rational map \(F_G\) are bounded by a common finite constant.  Taylor's formula, (13), and (14) therefore give uniformly
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sqrt N\{F_G(\widehat s)-F_G(s)\}
 &=J_F(s)\sqrt N(\widehat s-s)+O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\sqrt N\|\widehat s-s\|^2\right)\\
 &=\frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{i=1}^N J_F(s)Y_i+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\\
 &=\frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{IF}_F(X_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1). \tag{15}
 \end{aligned}
\]
The complement of the tube has probability tending to zero uniformly by (13), so the pole convention does not alter (15).

We verify the asserted uniform Gaussian limit directly.  Put \(Z_{\Sigma}=V_F(\Sigma)^{-1/2}\operatorname{IF}_F(X)\).  The chart condition gives \(\|V_F^{-1/2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\nu_{\mathrm{chart}}^{-1/2}\); boundedness of \(J_F\) and (12) give
\[
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\mathbb E_\Sigma\|Z_\Sigma\|^3<\infty,qquad
 \mathbb E_\Sigma Z_\Sigma=0,qquad
 \mathbb E_\Sigma Z_\Sigma Z_\Sigma^{\mathsf T}=I_r. \tag{16}
\]
For fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^r\), the inequality
\[
 \left|e^{ix}-1-ix+\frac{x^2}{2}\right|\leq\frac{|x|^3}{6}
\]
and (16) imply, uniformly in \(\Sigma\),
\[
 \mathbb E_\Sigma e^{it^{\mathsf T}Z_\Sigma/\sqrt N}
 =1-\frac{\|t\|^2}{2N}+O(N^{-3/2}).
\]
Raising this characteristic function to the \(N\)-th power gives \(\exp(-\|t\|^2/2)+o(1)\), uniformly.  Tightness follows from the identity covariance in (16), so every parameter sequence has the standard normal limit.  Undoing the standardization proves the uniform interpretation of
\[
 N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{IF}_F(X_i)\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,V_F). \tag{17}
\]

On the tube, define the plug-in influence vectors by
\[
 \widehat{\operatorname{IF}}_{i}
 =J_F(\widehat s)\operatorname{vech}(X_iX_i^{\mathsf T}-\widehat\Sigma).
\]
For each matrix entry, (12) with \(k=8\) and Chebyshev's inequality give a uniform law of large numbers for the empirical second moment of the oracle influence vectors.  The mean-value theorem, \(J_F(\widehat s)-J_F(s)=O_{\mathbb P}(\|\widehat s-s\|)\), and the same uniform moment bounds show that replacing \(J_F(s)\) and \(\Sigma\) by their sample analogues changes that empirical second moment by \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).  Hence
\[
 \widehat V_F\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}V_F \tag{18}
\]
uniformly on the chart.

By (14), a sample denominator pole is contained in \(\{\|\widehat s-s\|>\eta\}\), whose probability tends to zero uniformly.  By Weyl's eigenvalue inequality, on \(\{\|\widehat V_F-V_F\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\nu_{\mathrm{chart}}/2\}\),
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat V_F)\geq
 \lambda_{\min}(V_F)-\|\widehat V_F-V_F\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \geq\nu_{\mathrm{chart}}/2>0.
\]
Equation (18) therefore proves both exceptional-event assertions.

On their complement, (15), (17), (18), and continuity of matrix inversion give
\[
 N\{\widehat\theta_G-F_G(s)\}^{\mathsf T}\widehat V_F^{-1}
 \{\widehat\theta_G-F_G(s)\}\rightsquigarrow\chi_r^2
\]
uniformly.  The \(\chi_r^2\) distribution is continuous at \(\chi^2_{r,1-\gamma}\), while on either exceptional event the confidence set is \(\mathbb R^r\).  Since those events have uniformly vanishing probability, the infimal coverage converges to \(1-\gamma\).

Finally, distinguish the statistical functional from the structural target.  For a valid returned formula, its retained graph-ideal certificate is
\[
 qQ_{F,j}(s)-P_{F,j}(s)\in I_G.
\]
Substitution by \(\tau_G\) and the chart's nonzero denominator give \(q=P_{F,j}(s)/Q_{F,j}(s)\).  Coordinatewise, on a model covariance produced by the successful exact schedule,
\[
 \theta_G=F_G(\operatorname{vech}\Sigma).
\]
Thus the Wald set covers the structural vector only through this proved identifying equality; the probability argument itself targets the observable-law functional \(F_G(s)\).  No step asserts efficiency.
